issues.legal_issue: A final decree for sale in a redemption suit does not extinguish the mortgagor’s right of redemption or bar a later redemption suit unless the decree extinguishes that right in a manner recognized by law.
material_facts: A prior suit for redemption of the mortgages resulted in a preliminary decree and then a final decree for sale after the mortgagors failed to pay.
The mortgagee did not execute the final decree, and no sale was confirmed; the mortgagee and successors remained in possession of the property.
The mortgages were neither mortgages by conditional sale nor anomalous mortgages, and the final decree did not declare the mortgagors debarred from redemption.
The successors of the mortgagors brought a second suit for redemption within the limitation period.
issues.conclusion: The right of redemption was not extinguished by the earlier decrees, and the second suit for redemption was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act provides that the right of redemption is extinguished only by act of the parties or by a court decree. Under Order XXXIV, Rule 3(2), a foreclosure decree extinguishes redemption when it declares the mortgagor debarred; under Rule 8(3)(a), that declaration may be made in a final decree for redemption of a mortgage by conditional sale or an anomalous mortgage. Rules 5(1) and 8(1) recognize redemption before confirmation of sale in the circumstances they specify. The right can be taken away only by the means and in the manner prescribed: Raghunath Singh v. Mt. Hansraj Kunwar, AIR 1934 PC 205. The Court held erroneous the contrary merger reasoning in Sheo Narain Sah v. Mt. Deolochan Kuer, AIR 1948 Patna 208; a second suit within limitation is not barred where the right remains unextinguished.

rule.if: appeal_from_second_redemption_suit and prior_redemption_suit_final_decree and mortgage_not_conditional_or_anomalous and decree_did_not_expressly_bar_redemption and sale_not_confirmed and second_suit_within_limitation

predicates.appeal_from_second_redemption_suit: The case is an appeal arising from a later suit seeking redemption of a mortgage previously litigated.
predicates.prior_redemption_suit_final_decree: An earlier redemption suit resulted in a final decree for sale after the mortgagor failed to pay.
predicates.mortgage_not_conditional_or_anomalous: The mortgage was neither a mortgage by conditional sale nor an anomalous mortgage.
predicates.decree_did_not_expressly_bar_redemption: The final decree did not declare the mortgagor debarred from redeeming the property.
predicates.sale_not_confirmed: A sale under the final decree had not been confirmed.
predicates.second_suit_within_limitation: The later redemption suit was brought within the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a later redemption suit, the earlier decree did not expressly bar redemption, and the unconfirmed sale and timely filing leave the right alive, the later suit is maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: The equitable rule limiting recoverable interest to the principal applies to mortgage transactions that are governed by that rule.
material_facts: The redemption suit required the court to calculate the sums due under mortgages that secured loans and transferred interests in immovable property.
The lower court applied the Damdupat rule when calculating interest, and the appellants challenged its application to mortgages.
issues.conclusion: The Damdupat rule applies to mortgages, and its application to the interest calculation was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Damdupat rule is an equitable rule that prevents a creditor from recovering, at a given time, interest exceeding the principal then due. Because a mortgage is principally a loan transaction as well as a transfer of an interest in immovable property, the rule may apply to a mortgage. The Court disapproved Madhwa Sidhanta Onahini Nidhi v. Venkataramanjulu Naidu, ILR 26 Madras 662, and approved Kunja Lal Banerji v. Narsamba Debi, ILR 42 Cal. 826; Jeewan Bai v. Monordas Lachmondas, ILR 35 Bom. 199; and Bapurao v. Anant Kashinath, AIR 1946 Nagpur 210. The judgment notes that the rule was not applicable in Madras.

predicates.mortgage_redemption_accounting_dispute: The proceeding concerns calculation of the amount payable to redeem a mortgage.
predicates.mortgage_is_a_loan_transaction: The mortgage secures a loan while also transferring an interest in immovable property.
predicates.damdupat_rule_governs_the_transaction: The transaction is governed by a legal tradition in which the Damdupat rule applies.

issues.definition: When a mortgage redemption accounting dispute involves a loan transaction governed by the Damdupat rule, that rule applies to the mortgage interest.
